comparator.name: Bachelor in Criminology
comparator.sourceNotes: The official current 2027–2028 brochure curriculum specifies a fixed 180-EC three-year bachelor: criminological and social-science foundations, legal study, two methods courses, three Research Lab stages, advanced criminology and criminal-law courses, a 15-EC minor, prevention and law-enforcement study, European justice, migration/diversity/crime, and a 15-EC analysis-and-reporting component. There are no formal bachelor routes requiring selection. The visible current table on brochure page 3 was inspected, rather than combining hidden older PDF text layers. The current study page corroborates Empirical legal studies (6 EC), Research Lab - de basis (7 EC), and the single 15-EC analysis/reporting component. The third-year skills strand combines the 6-EC application lab with the 15-EC analysis/reporting component; no extra thesis is added. The minor remains open and no formal route is imposed. The former 2026–2027 brochure URL now redirects to the 2027–2028 edition. The external curriculum year follows that actual edition, independently of the UCR workbook planning terms.

alternatives.labelRationale: The institutional and normative emphasis is implemented by constitutional and criminal law, rights, political philosophy, EU politics, ethics and public economics. No dedicated public-safety planning or crime-policy evaluation sequence is claimed.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Political philosophy, EU politics, Public Economics and Ethics replace Abnormal Psychology, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Advanced Research Seminar and Youth Resilience to Extremism. The four-course/30-EC difference shifts the organising inquiry from behavioural explanation and prevention applications toward public authority, institutional legality and normative judgment.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One additional evidenced institutional/legal direction is feasible and differs by four courses/30 EC. A separate victimisation/support direction was considered: human rights, social psychology and media/race supply particular perspectives but do not establish a materially distinct, sustained 24-course victimology/support programme from the current catalogue. No third option is manufactured. Crime-prevention interest 18 is assigned to the closest option, which actually includes the youth-resilience application; specialist crime-prevention and victimology limits remain explicit.

notes.text: Erasmus Criminology has a dedicated sequence in criminological theory, crime measurement and harm, criminal careers, Dutch criminal procedure/substantive law, law enforcement and mixed-methods research. UCR offers related socio-legal, psychological and empirical study, including actual criminal-law and organised-crime content, but does not reproduce that complete disciplinary sequence, specialised victimology/support training or the 21-EC final research strand. General EU law, psychology and evidence synthesis remain complementary perspectives.

audience.programmeDescription: Criminology at Erasmus University Rotterdam studies how crime is defined, explained and addressed, and how it affects people and society. The programme combines criminological theory, social science, law and empirical research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Two UCR programmes offer related study through crime, society and justice, or through law and public authority. They combine criminal-law content with wider legal, social-science and research perspectives. Dedicated criminological theory, crime measurement, criminal careers, Dutch criminal procedure and the complete final research strand remain differences.

curriculum.limitation: The complete 180-EC curriculum includes a 15-EC open minor and a final research strand comprising Research Lab - de toepassing (6 EC) and Onderzoeksvaardigheden: analyse en rapportage (15 EC). No minor subject or specialisation is assumed.
